text: The Patriots are navigating a pivotal moment after Drake Maye's triumphant rebound against Buffalo—a three-touchdown performance that earned him AFC Offensive Player of the Week honors and delivered New England a critical 29-26 upset victory over the Bills that head coach Mike Vrabel emphasized as essential for the defending AFC champions' trajectory. However, optimism is tempered by uncertainty at running back, where Rhamondre Stevenson's injury leaves the team facing real questions about depth at the position as they prepare to host the Raiders on Sunday at Gillette Stadium. The defensive unit showed it can still execute when called upon, shutting down the Bills' red-hot tight end Dalton Kincaid in Week 4, though the Raiders present a more complicated matchup with their one-two tight end punch of Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer that will test the secondary and linebacker corps. While some observers are already ready to pronounce the Patriots back on track at 2-2 after a stunning Week 4 rally that mirrored similar comebacks by the Rams and Cowboys, the beat is appropriately cautious about whether this represents genuine resurgence or an outlier performance from a team still searching for consistency in the early going.
